AMGN.rationale: Amgen shows solid fundamental health with strong revenue growth (10% YoY in 2025, 5.8% YoY in Q1 2026), broad-based product momentum (16 brands with double-digit growth, 17 products annualizing >$1B), and robust cash generation ($1.5B free cash flow in Q1 2026 vs $1.0B prior year). The balance sheet carries significant debt ($54.6B) with a debt-to-equity of 8.0x, which is elevated but manageable given strong operating cash flows ($4.68B in latest quarter). The company is executing well on its diversified portfolio strategy across oncology, inflammation, rare disease, and general medicine, with biosimilars contributing $3B in 2025 (up 37%). However, valuation is stretched: the P/E of 44.4x is near the top of its 33.6-49.7x range over the past year, and P/B of 24.9x is also elevated. The stock has re-rated significantly from ~36x P/E in mid-2025 to 44x+ currently, pricing in much of the growth. Key risks include the Tavneos FDA withdrawal concern, patent expirations on legacy products, and the competitive challenge of MariTide entering a GLP-1 dominated obesity market. The Q1 2026 earnings beat on EPS ($5.15 vs $4.73-$4.85 est) but slight revenue miss ($8.62B vs $8.75B est) and raised guidance provide a modest near-term positive, but the stock's after-market reaction was mixed. Net-net: good business trajectory but valuation leaves limited margin of safety.
